people.name: Solomon
people.role: King building and dedicating the temple
people.relations: Son of David and Bathsheba. Father of Rehoboam.
people.meaning: He asks God for wisdom at Gibeon. He builds the temple with help from Huram of Tyre. He prays at its dedication, and fire comes down from heaven. Hezekiah’s Passover joy is the greatest in Jerusalem since his time.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: David
people.role: Earlier king whose plans and promise guide later kings
people.relations: Son of Jesse. Father of Amnon, Absalom, Tamar, Solomon, and other children.
people.meaning: Solomon is already king in his place when the book opens. Solomon builds the temple on the site David chose. Later kings follow his orders for priests, Levites, and music. God keeps David’s house because of the covenant with him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Moses
people.role: Earlier leader whose law guides temple worship
people.relations: Son of Amram and Jochebed. Brother of Aaron and Miriam. Husband of Zipporah.
people.meaning: He made the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness. He put the two tablets in the ark at Horeb. Later kings and priests follow his law for offerings, a tax, and Passover.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Bezalel
people.role: Maker of the bronze altar at Gibeon
people.relations: Son of Uri. Grandson of Hur. Member of Judah's tribe.
people.meaning: He made the bronze altar that stands at Gibeon. Solomon offers one thousand burnt offerings on it. The book names him only here.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hiram
people.role: King of Tyre who sends timber and sailors
people.relations: This book calls him Huram. He sent cedars to David and now deals with Solomon.
people.meaning: Solomon asks him for timber and a skilled worker. Huram answers in writing and blesses the LORD. He sends Huram-abi, and wood by sea to Joppa. Later his sailors go with Solomon’s servants to Ophir for gold.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Huram-abi / Hiram, the craft worker
people.role: Craftsman making temple furnishings
people.relations: Son of a woman of Dan and a man of Tyre (2:14). Kings words his mother’s family differently.
people.meaning: Huram the king sends him to Solomon. He makes the pillars, the sea, the pots, and other bronze vessels. He is not King Huram, though 4:11 calls him Huram.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ornan / Araunah
people.role: Ornan, Jebusite owner of the threshing floor
people.relations: A Jebusite. The place David chose for the temple was his threshing floor.
people.meaning: This book calls him Ornan. Solomon builds the LORD’s house on his threshing floor on Mount Moriah. David had chosen that place. This book does not tell how David got it.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Asaph, the singer
people.role: Singer whose family leads temple music
people.relations: Son of Berechiah. Leads a musical family.
people.meaning: He stands with the singers when the ark enters the temple. Jahaziel, from his family, speaks before Jehoshaphat’s battle. Hezekiah’s Levites sing his words, and the book calls him a seer. His sons sing at Josiah’s Passover.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Heman, the singer
people.role: Singer whose sons serve in the temple
people.relations: He stands with Asaph and Jeduthun. His sons Jehuel and Shimei serve under Hezekiah.
people.meaning: He sings with cymbals and harps when the ark enters the temple. His sons help cleanse the temple for Hezekiah. Josiah’s singers follow his command.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jeduthun
people.role: Singer called the king’s seer
people.relations: He stands with Asaph and Heman. His sons Shemaiah and Uzziel serve under Hezekiah.
people.meaning: He sings when the ark enters the temple. His sons help cleanse the temple for Hezekiah. In 35:15 the book calls him the king’s seer.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pharaoh’s daughter, Solomon’s wife
people.role: Unnamed Egyptian wife of Solomon
people.relations: Wife of Solomon. Distinct from the princess who finds Moses in Exodus.
people.meaning: Solomon moves her out of David’s city to a house he built for her. He says the places the ark has come are holy. She says and does nothing in the account.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The queen of Sheba
people.role: Unnamed queen who tests Solomon with questions
people.relations: She rules Sheba. She meets Solomon in Jerusalem.
people.meaning: She comes with camels, spices, gold, and precious stones. Solomon answers all her hard questions. She says the report was true and blesses the LORD. They trade gifts, and she goes home.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nathan
people.role: Earlier prophet named in records and music orders
people.relations: Named with Ahijah and Iddo in 9:29. Named with David and Gad in 29:25.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. His history is one record of Solomon’s reign. Hezekiah places the Levite players as David, Gad, and Nathan commanded.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahijah, the Shilonite
people.role: Prophet whose word to Jeroboam comes true
people.relations: From Shiloh. He spoke the LORD’s word to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
people.meaning: He does not appear in person. His prophecy is one record of Solomon’s reign. When Rehoboam refuses the people, the book says the LORD’s word by Ahijah stands.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Iddo, the seer
people.role: Seer whose writings record three kings
people.relations: The book names his writings for Solomon, Rehoboam, and Abijah.
people.meaning: He does not act in the account. His visions about Jeroboam record Solomon’s acts. His other writings record Rehoboam and Abijah. Chapter 13 calls him a prophet.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jeroboam
people.role: First king of the northern tribes
people.relations: Son of Nebat and the widow Zeruah. Father of Abijah and Nadab.
people.meaning: He returns from Egypt and asks Rehoboam to lighten the people’s load. Israel leaves Rehoboam, and Jeroboam rules the north. He casts off the Levites and makes calf idols. Abijah defeats him, and the LORD strikes him dead.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Rehoboam
people.role: King whose harsh answer divides the kingdom
people.relations: Son of Solomon and Naamah the Ammonitess. Father of Abijah.
people.meaning: He answers the people roughly, and most of Israel leaves him. Shemaiah stops him from fighting to win them back. He builds strong cities, then abandons the LORD’s law. Shishak takes the treasures, but Rehoboam humbles himself and is not destroyed.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hadoram / Adoram
people.role: Forced-labor officer stoned by Israel
people.relations: This book calls him Hadoram. Rehoboam sends him to the children of Israel.
people.meaning: He is over the men forced to work. Rehoboam sends him after Israel leaves. The people stone him to death, and Rehoboam flees to Jerusalem.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jesse
people.role: Father of David
people.relations: Father of Eliab, Abinadab, Shammah, David, and other sons.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. All Israel calls David “the son of Jesse” when they leave Rehoboam. Chapter 11 names him as the father of Eliab.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shemaiah
people.role: Man of God who speaks to Rehoboam twice
people.relations: He speaks to Rehoboam, Judah, and the princes. His histories record Rehoboam’s acts.
people.meaning: He tells Rehoboam’s army not to fight Israel, and the men go home. When Shishak attacks, he says Judah has left the LORD. The king and princes humble themselves. Shemaiah then says the LORD will not destroy them.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Mahalath
people.role: Wife of Rehoboam
people.relations: Daughter of Jerimoth and Abihail. Mother of Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
people.meaning: Rehoboam takes her as a wife. She bears him Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham. The book tells nothing more about her.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abihail, Mahalath’s mother
people.role: Woman named in Rehoboam’s family record
people.relations: Daughter of Eliab, the son of Jesse. Mother of Mahalath.
people.meaning: The book names her once, in Rehoboam’s family record. Her daughter Mahalath marries Rehoboam. Her father Eliab is a son of Jesse.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Maacah
people.role: Queen mother removed by Asa
people.relations: Granddaughter of Absalom and wife of Rehoboam. The text calls her mother of Abijah and of Asa.
people.meaning: Rehoboam loves her above all his wives and makes her son Abijah chief. Later she makes an image for an Asherah. Asa removes her as queen mother. He cuts down the image and burns it at the brook Kidron.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abijah / Abijam
people.role: King of Judah who defeats Jeroboam
people.relations: Son of Rehoboam. Chapter 11 names his mother Maacah, but 13:2 names Micaiah.
people.meaning: This book calls him Abijah. He stands on Mount Zemaraim and tells Israel not to fight the LORD. Jeroboam’s men trap Judah front and back. Judah cries to the LORD and wins, and Abijah takes Bethel.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shishak
people.role: Egyptian king who attacks Jerusalem
people.relations: King of Egypt. He comes against Rehoboam in the king’s fifth year.
people.meaning: He takes Judah’s strong cities and comes to Jerusalem. He carries off the temple and palace treasures. He also takes Solomon’s gold shields. The LORD does not let him destroy Jerusalem.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Naamah
people.role: Ammonite mother of Rehoboam
people.relations: An Ammonitess. Named once, at the end of Rehoboam’s reign.
people.meaning: The book gives only her name and her people. She does nothing in the account.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Aaron
people.role: Earlier priest whose sons serve at the altar
people.relations: Son of Amram and Jochebed. Father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. His sons are the priests who burn incense and offer sacrifices. Abijah says Jeroboam drove them out. Azariah tells Uzziah that only they may burn incense.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Asa
people.role: King who trusts God, then turns to Syria
people.relations: Son of Abijah. Father of Jehoshaphat.
people.meaning: He removes foreign altars and calls on the LORD against Zerah’s army. After Azariah’s words, he leads Judah into a covenant. Later he pays Ben Hadad to attack Baasha. He jails the seer Hanani and seeks only doctors when sick.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zerah, the Cushite
people.role: Leader of the army Asa meets at Mareshah
people.relations: The reading translation calls him the Ethiopian. It names no family.
people.meaning: He comes to Mareshah with a million troops and three hundred chariots. Asa prays, and the LORD strikes Zerah’s army. Judah chases them to Gerar and takes much plunder.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Azariah, son of Oded
people.role: Prophet who speaks to Asa
people.relations: Son of Oded. He is not King Uzziah or any priest named Azariah.
people.meaning: The Spirit of God comes on him, and he goes to meet Asa. He says the LORD is with those who seek him. He tells Asa to be strong. Asa takes courage and renews the LORD’s altar.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Oded, Azariah’s father
people.role: Father of the prophet Azariah
people.relations: Father of Azariah in 15:1. Verse 8 speaks of “the prophecy of Oded the prophet.”
people.meaning: He does nothing in the account. Verse 8 gives the prophecy his name, not his son’s. The text does not explain the difference.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Baasha
people.role: King of Israel who builds Ramah against Judah
people.relations: Son of Ahijah of the house of Issachar. Father of Elah.
people.meaning: He builds Ramah so no one can go in or out to Asa. Asa pays Ben Hadad to break his treaty with Baasha. Syria strikes Israel’s cities, and Baasha stops building. Asa carries away the stones and timber.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ben Hadad, Asa’s ally
people.role: King of Syria paid to attack Israel
people.relations: Son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion.
people.meaning: He lives at Damascus and has a treaty with Baasha. Asa sends him silver and gold from the temple. He sends his captains against Ijon, Dan, and Abel Maim. A later Ben Hadad fights Ahab in Kings.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hanani, the seer
people.role: Seer who warns Asa about Syria
people.relations: He speaks to Asa. Jehu the son of Hanani speaks to Jehoshaphat in chapter 19.
people.meaning: He tells Asa he relied on Syria’s king and not on the LORD. He reminds Asa of the win over the Ethiopians. He says Asa will now have wars. Asa is angry and puts him in prison.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.role: King who sends teachers, appoints judges, and prays
people.relations: Son of Asa and Azubah. Father of Jehoram.
people.meaning: He sends princes, Levites, and priests to teach the law in Judah. He joins Ahab’s war, and Jehu the son of Hanani corrects him. He appoints judges and prays when three armies come. His ships with Ahaziah are wrecked.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Amasiah, son of Zichri
people.role: Captain who offers himself to the LORD
people.relations: Son of Zichri. One of Jehoshaphat’s captains from Judah.
people.meaning: He leads two hundred thousand mighty men. The book says he willingly offered himself to the LORD. It tells nothing more about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahab
people.role: King of Israel who dies at Ramoth Gilead
people.relations: King of Israel and ally of Jehoshaphat. His daughter marries Jehoram of Judah.
people.meaning: He asks Jehoshaphat to fight for Ramoth Gilead. He jails Micaiah for saying he will fall. He goes into battle in disguise, but an arrow strikes him. He dies at sunset, and his house later leads Judah’s kings astray.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Micaiah
people.role: Prophet who tells Ahab he will fall
people.relations: Son of Imla. Ahab hates him and sends him to prison.
people.meaning: A messenger asks him to agree with the other prophets. He says he will speak what God says. He tells of Israel scattered and a lying spirit in the prophets. Zedekiah strikes him, and Ahab jails him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zedekiah
people.role: Prophet who opposes Micaiah
people.relations: Son of Chenaanah. One of Ahab’s prophets.
people.meaning: He makes iron horns and says Ahab will push the Syrians. He strikes Micaiah on the cheek. Micaiah says he will hide in an inner room. He is not the later king of Judah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Amon
people.role: City governor ordered to hold Micaiah
people.relations: Governor of the city. Named with Joash the king’s son.
people.meaning: Ahab orders Micaiah taken back to him. He is to keep Micaiah in prison on bread and water. He is not Amon, the later king of Judah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joash
people.role: King’s son named in Micaiah’s imprisonment order
people.relations: Called the king’s son. Named with Amon the governor.
people.meaning: Ahab orders Micaiah taken to him and to Amon. They are to hold Micaiah until Ahab returns. He is not Joash king of Judah or Joash king of Israel.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The prophets who counsel Ahab
people.role: Four hundred prophets who promise Ahab victory
people.relations: Four hundred men gathered by Ahab. Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah speaks among them.
people.meaning: Ahab asks them if he should go to Ramoth Gilead. They all say God will give it to the king. Micaiah says a lying spirit speaks through them. Ahab dies in the battle.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehu, Hanani’s son
people.role: Seer’s son who corrects Jehoshaphat
people.relations: Son of Hanani the seer. He is not Jehu the son of Nimshi.
people.meaning: He meets Jehoshaphat after the war with Ahab. He asks why the king helps the wicked. He also says good things are found in him. His history records Jehoshaphat’s acts.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Amariah, the chief priest
people.role: Chief priest over matters of the LORD
people.relations: Named with Zebadiah in Jehoshaphat’s appointments.
people.meaning: Jehoshaphat sets him over the Jerusalem judges in all matters of the LORD. Zebadiah has the king’s matters. The book tells nothing more about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zebadiah, son of Ishmael
people.role: Ruler over the king’s matters in court
people.relations: Son of Ishmael and ruler of the house of Judah. Named with Amariah.
people.meaning: Jehoshaphat sets him over the judges in all the king’s matters. Amariah has the matters of the LORD. The king tells them all to act with courage.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jahaziel, the Levite
people.role: Levite who speaks before Jehoshaphat’s battle
people.relations: Descendant of Asaph through Zechariah, Benaiah, Jeiel, and Mattaniah.
people.meaning: The LORD’s Spirit comes on him in the assembly. He tells Judah not to fear, for the battle is God’s. He says where the enemy will be. Jehoshaphat bows down, and the army goes out singing.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Azubah, Jehoshaphat’s mother
people.role: Mother of Jehoshaphat
people.relations: Daughter of Shilhi and mother of Jehoshaphat.
people.meaning: The book names her once, at the end of Jehoshaphat’s reign. She does nothing in the account.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahaziah
people.role: King of Israel who builds ships with Jehoshaphat
people.relations: Son of Ahab.
people.meaning: The book says he did very wickedly. Jehoshaphat joins him to build ships at Ezion Geber. The ships are wrecked. He is not Ahaziah king of Judah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Eliezer, son of Dodavahu
people.role: Prophet who speaks against the ships
people.relations: Son of Dodavahu, from Mareshah. He speaks against Jehoshaphat.
people.meaning: He says the LORD has destroyed Jehoshaphat’s works for joining Ahaziah. The ships are wrecked and cannot go to Tarshish.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abraham
people.role: Earlier ancestor remembered as God’s friend
people.relations: Husband of Sarah. Father of Ishmael and Isaac. Uncle of Lot.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. Jehoshaphat prays that God gave the land to Abraham’s offspring. He calls Abraham God’s friend. Hezekiah’s letters call the LORD the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoram, king of Judah
people.role: King of Judah who kills his brothers
people.relations: Son of Jehoshaphat. Husband of Ahab’s daughter. Father of Ahaziah.
people.meaning: He kills all his brothers with the sword. Edom and Libnah revolt from him. A letter from Elijah warns of plague and sickness. Raiders carry off his family, and he dies of a bowel disease.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Elijah
people.role: Prophet whose letter warns Jehoram
people.relations: Called Elijah the prophet. His letter comes to Jehoram king of Judah.
people.meaning: His letter says Jehoram walked like Israel’s kings and killed his brothers. It warns of a plague on his people and family. It says Jehoram will have a bowel disease. Each thing then happens.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahaziah, king of Judah
people.role: King of Judah killed by Jehu
people.relations: Youngest son of Jehoram and Athaliah, and father of Joash. Also called Jehoahaz (21:17) and Azariah (22:6).
people.meaning: Jerusalem’s people make him king after raiders kill his older brothers. His mother counsels him to do evil. He visits the wounded Joram, and Jehu kills him. The text gives his age as forty-two, but 2 Kings 8:26 says twenty-two.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joram, king of Israel
people.role: King of Israel wounded fighting Hazael
people.relations: Son of Ahab. The text calls him both Jehoram and Joram.
people.meaning: He fights Hazael at Ramoth Gilead, and the Syrians wound him. He goes to Jezreel to heal. Ahaziah of Judah visits him there. He is not Jehoram king of Judah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Athaliah
people.role: Royal woman who seizes Judah’s throne
people.relations: Mother of Ahaziah. The text calls her the daughter of Omri.
people.meaning: She counsels her son Ahaziah to do evil. When he dies, she kills the royal children and reigns six years. Jehoiada crowns Joash, and she cries, “Treason!” The captains kill her at the horse gate.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Omri
people.role: Name in Athaliah’s family record
people.relations: Athaliah is called the daughter of Omri. Kings names him as Ahab’s father.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. The book names him once, in Ahaziah’s record.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hazael
people.role: King of Syria who fights Israel and Judah
people.relations: King of Syria. He fights Jehoram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah.
people.meaning: He fights at Ramoth Gilead against Jehoram and Ahaziah. His Syrians wound Jehoram. The book names him only in chapter 22.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehu, Nimshi’s son
people.role: Man anointed to cut off Ahab’s house
people.relations: Son of Nimshi and grandfather of Joash king of Israel. He is not Jehu the son of Hanani.
people.meaning: The LORD anoints him to cut off Ahab’s house. He kills the princes of Judah who serve Ahaziah. His men find Ahaziah hiding in Samaria, and Ahaziah is killed.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoshabeath / Jehosheba
people.role: Royal woman who rescues the infant Joash
people.relations: Daughter of King Jehoram, sister of Ahaziah, and wife of Jehoiada the priest.
people.meaning: This book calls her Jehoshabeath. She takes the child Joash from among the king’s sons being killed. She hides him and his nurse in a bedroom. He stays hidden in God’s house six years.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joash’s nurse
people.role: Unnamed caregiver hidden with the child
people.relations: Nurse of Joash. Jehoshabeath hides her with the child.
people.meaning: Jehoshabeath puts her and Joash in a bedroom. The book says nothing more about her.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joash, king of Judah
people.role: Hidden child king who later kills Zechariah
people.relations: Son of Ahaziah and Zibiah. Father of Amaziah. Also called Jehoash.
people.meaning: He is hidden six years and crowned at age seven. He has a chest made and repairs the temple. After Jehoiada dies, he listens to the princes and serves idols. He has Zechariah stoned, and his own servants kill him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoiada
people.role: Priest who crowns Joash and guides him
people.relations: Husband of Jehoshabeath and father of Zechariah. He raises and guides Joash.
people.meaning: He arms the captains and Levites and crowns Joash in the temple. He orders Athaliah killed outside the LORD’s house. He makes a covenant and helps repair the temple. He dies at 130 and is buried among the kings.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Mattan
people.role: Priest of Baal killed at his altars
people.relations: Priest of Baal. The people kill him after Joash is crowned.
people.meaning: The people break down the house of Baal after the covenant. They smash its altars and images. They kill Mattan before the altars.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zibiah
people.role: Mother of Joash king of Judah
people.relations: From Beersheba. Mother of Joash of Judah.
people.meaning: The book names her once, as the mother of Joash. She comes from Beersheba.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zechariah, son of Jehoiada
people.role: Prophet killed after correcting Joash
people.relations: Son of Jehoiada the priest. Joash orders his death.
people.meaning: The Spirit of God comes on him. He tells the people they left the LORD, so the LORD left them. They stone him in the temple court at the king’s command. Dying, he asks the LORD to see and repay.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zabad, son of Shimeath
people.role: Servant who helps kill Joash
people.relations: Son of Shimeath the Ammonitess.
people.meaning: He and Jehozabad plot against Joash for the blood of Jehoiada’s sons. They kill the wounded king on his bed. Kings gives him a different name.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehozabad
people.role: Servant who helps kill Joash
people.relations: Son of Shimrith the Moabitess (24:26). Kings spells his mother’s name differently.
people.meaning: He and Zabad plot against Joash after Zechariah’s death. They kill the wounded king on his bed. Amaziah later kills the servants who did it.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Amaziah
people.role: King who defeats Edom and loses to Israel
people.relations: Son of Joash and Jehoaddan. Father of Uzziah.
people.meaning: He sends home the hired soldiers of Israel when a man of God warns him. He defeats Edom but brings back its gods. He challenges Joash of Israel and loses at Beth Shemesh. Plotters later kill him at Lachish.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoaddan
people.role: Mother of Amaziah
people.relations: From Jerusalem. Mother of Amaziah.
people.meaning: The book names her once, as Amaziah’s mother. She comes from Jerusalem.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joash, king of Israel
people.role: King of Israel who defeats Amaziah
people.relations: Son of Jehoahaz and grandson of Jehu. He is not Joash king of Judah.
people.meaning: Amaziah dares him to meet face to face. He answers with a story of a thistle and a cedar. He defeats Judah at Beth Shemesh and captures Amaziah. He breaks Jerusalem’s wall and takes the temple gold to Samaria.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoahaz, king of Israel
people.role: Father of Joash king of Israel
people.relations: Son of Jehu. Father of Joash.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. Chapter 25 names him as the father of Joash king of Israel. He is not Josiah’s son Jehoahaz in chapter 36.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The man of God advising Amaziah
people.role: Unnamed man of God against the hired troops
people.relations: He speaks to Amaziah before the fight with Edom.
people.meaning: He tells Amaziah not to take Israel’s army, for the LORD is not with Israel. Amaziah asks about the hundred talents he paid. The man says the LORD can give much more. Amaziah sends the soldiers home.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The prophet warning Amaziah
people.role: Unnamed prophet who questions Amaziah’s new gods
people.relations: The LORD sends him to Amaziah after the win over Edom.
people.meaning: He asks why Amaziah seeks gods that could not save their own people. The king tells him to stop or be struck down. He stops, but says God has decided to destroy Amaziah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Obed-Edom, the temple custodian
people.role: Man named with the seized temple vessels
people.relations: Named once, in 25:24, in Amaziah’s reign.
people.meaning: The gold, silver, and vessels in God’s house are “with Obed-Edom.” Joash of Israel takes them all to Samaria. The text says nothing more about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Uzziah / Azariah
people.role: Uzziah, king struck with leprosy over incense
people.relations: Son of Amaziah. Father of Jotham.
people.meaning: He seeks God in the days of Zechariah, and God makes him prosper. He builds towers, digs cisterns, and arms a large army. When he is strong, he goes into the temple to burn incense. Leprosy breaks out on his forehead, and he lives apart until death.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jechiliah
people.role: Mother of Uzziah
people.relations: From Jerusalem. Named in Uzziah’s reign notice.
people.meaning: The book names her once, as Uzziah’s mother. She comes from Jerusalem.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zechariah, Uzziah’s adviser
people.role: Guide in Uzziah’s early years
people.relations: The book says he had understanding in the vision of God.
people.meaning: Uzziah sets himself to seek God in Zechariah’s days. The book gives no words or acts of his. He is not Zechariah the son of Jehoiada.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Azariah, the priest opposing Uzziah
people.role: Chief priest who stops Uzziah’s incense
people.relations: Chief priest. Eighty priests go in with him against the king.
people.meaning: He follows Uzziah into the temple with eighty priests. They tell the king that only Aaron’s sons may burn incense. They see leprosy on his forehead and thrust him out. He is not the chief priest Azariah of Hezekiah’s day.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jotham
people.role: King of Judah who builds and grows strong
people.relations: Son of Uzziah. Father of Ahaz.
people.meaning: He judges the people while his father Uzziah is a leper. As king he builds the temple’s upper gate, cities, and towers. He defeats Ammon and receives silver, wheat, and barley. He does right, but the people still act corruptly.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Isaiah
people.role: Prophet who prays with Hezekiah
people.relations: Son of Amoz.
people.meaning: He writes the acts of Uzziah. He prays with Hezekiah when Sennacherib’s men mock the LORD. The LORD then sends an angel against Assyria’s camp. His vision also records Hezekiah’s acts.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jerushah
people.role: Mother of Jotham
people.relations: Daughter of Zadok. The text does not say this is David’s priest Zadok.
people.meaning: The book names her once, as Jotham’s mother. She does nothing in the account.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahaz
people.role: King of Judah who shuts the temple
people.relations: Son of Jotham. Father of Hezekiah.
people.meaning: He makes images for the Baals and burns his children in the fire. Syria, Israel, Edom, and the Philistines defeat Judah. He pays Assyria’s king, who gives him trouble instead of help. He then shuts the temple doors and worships the gods of Damascus.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pekah
people.role: King of Israel who strikes Judah
people.relations: Son of Remaliah. He fights Ahaz of Judah.
people.meaning: He kills one hundred twenty thousand men of Judah in one day. Israel’s army then carries off two hundred thousand captives. The book says Judah had left the LORD.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pul / Tiglath Pileser
people.role: Assyrian ruler whom Ahaz asks for help
people.relations: King of Assyria. This book spells his name Tilgath-pilneser (28:20).
people.meaning: Ahaz sends to Assyria for help against Edom and the Philistines. Tilgath-pilneser comes but gives him trouble. Ahaz gives him treasure from the temple and palace. It does not help.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Oded, the prophet at Samaria
people.role: Prophet who tells Israel to free captives
people.relations: A prophet of the LORD at Samaria. He is not Oded, Azariah’s father.
people.meaning: He meets Israel’s army as it brings Judah’s captives to Samaria. He says they killed in a rage that reached heaven. He tells them to send the captives back. Four leaders agree, and the captives go home.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The four leaders who care for captives
people.role: Four leaders of Ephraim who free the captives
people.relations: Azariah is Johanan’s son. Berechiah is Meshillemoth’s son. Jehizkiah is Shallum’s son. Amasa is Hadlai’s son.
people.meaning: They stand against the army and refuse the captives. They clothe the naked, feed them, and anoint them. They carry the weak on donkeys to Jericho. Then they return to Samaria.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hezekiah
people.role: King who reopens the temple and keeps Passover
people.relations: Son of Ahaz and Abijah. Father of Manasseh.
people.meaning: He opens the temple doors and has the Levites cleanse it. He invites Israel and Judah to Passover and prays for the unclean. He stops the springs and prays when Sennacherib comes. Later his heart is proud, but he humbles himself.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abijah / Abi, Hezekiah’s mother
people.role: Mother of Hezekiah
people.relations: Daughter of Zechariah. Mother of Hezekiah.
people.meaning: This book calls her Abijah. It names her once, as Hezekiah’s mother. She is not King Abijah, Rehoboam’s son.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Gad
people.role: Earlier seer named in Hezekiah’s music orders
people.relations: Called the king’s seer. Named with David and Nathan the prophet.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. Hezekiah sets the Levites with cymbals and harps as David, Gad, and Nathan commanded. The book says the command came from the LORD by his prophets.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Isaac
people.role: Earlier ancestor named in Hezekiah’s letters
people.relations: Husband of Rebekah. Father of Esau and Jacob.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. Hezekiah’s letters call the LORD the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. The letters ask the northern tribes to turn back to that God.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Azariah, Hezekiah’s chief priest
people.role: Chief priest who explains the heaps of offerings
people.relations: Of the house of Zadok. Called ruler of God’s house under Hezekiah.
people.meaning: Hezekiah asks about the heaps of offerings. Azariah says the priests have eaten enough and have plenty left. He and Hezekiah appoint men to oversee the stores. He is not the Azariah who opposed Uzziah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Conaniah, the Levite
people.role: Supervisor of temple supplies
people.relations: A Levite. His brother Shimei is second to him.
people.meaning: He rules over the offerings, tithes, and dedicated things brought to the temple. Ten overseers work under him and Shimei. Hezekiah and Azariah appoint them.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shimei, Conaniah’s brother
people.role: Second over the temple stores
people.relations: Brother of Conaniah the Levite. He serves under Hezekiah.
people.meaning: He is second to Conaniah over the offerings and tithes. Ten overseers work under the two brothers. The book tells nothing more about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Kore, son of Imnah
people.role: Gatekeeper who gives out the free will offerings
people.relations: Son of Imnah the Levite. Gatekeeper at the east gate.
people.meaning: He is over the free will offerings of God. He gives out the LORD’s offerings and the most holy things. Six men under him give shares in the priests’ cities.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Sennacherib
people.role: King of Assyria who threatens Jerusalem
people.relations: King of Assyria. His own children kill him in the house of his god.
people.meaning: He camps against Judah’s strong cities and attacks Lachish. His servants and letters say no god can save Jerusalem. An angel cuts down his mighty men, and he goes home in shame. His own royal record also tells of a war in Judah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Manasseh, king of Judah
people.role: King of Judah who humbles himself in Babylon
people.relations: Son of Hezekiah and Hephzibah. Father of Amon.
people.meaning: He rebuilds the high places and sets an idol in God’s house. Assyria’s captains take him in chains to Babylon. He humbles himself and prays, and God brings him back. Then he removes the idols and builds up the LORD’s altar.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Amon, king of Judah
people.role: King of Judah who does not humble himself
people.relations: Son of Manasseh and Meshullemeth. Father of Josiah.
people.meaning: He sacrifices to the images his father Manasseh made. He does not humble himself as Manasseh did. His servants kill him in his own house after two years. The people of the land make his son Josiah king.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Josiah
people.role: King renewing worship after the law book is found
people.relations: Son of Amon and Jedidah. Father of Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim.
people.meaning: He breaks down altars and images in Judah and beyond. He repairs the temple, hears the law book, and tears his clothes. He makes a covenant and keeps a great Passover. He ignores Neco’s warning and is shot at Megiddo.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hilkiah, the high priest
people.role: High priest who finds the book of the law
people.relations: He works with Shaphan. He goes with the king’s men to Huldah.
people.meaning: He finds the book of the LORD’s law while money is brought out. He gives it to Shaphan. He leads the king’s men to Huldah. At Passover he gives animals to the priests.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shaphan
people.role: Scribe who reads the book to Josiah
people.relations: Son of Azaliah. Father of Ahikam.
people.meaning: Josiah sends him to repair the temple. Hilkiah gives him the book of the law. He reports on the work and reads the book to the king. Then he goes with the others to Huldah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Huldah
people.role: Prophetess asked about the book of the law
people.relations: Wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe. She lives in Jerusalem’s second quarter.
people.meaning: Josiah’s men come to ask her about the book. She says the LORD will bring its curses on Jerusalem. She says Josiah will go to his grave in peace before that evil. The men carry her message to the king.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shallum, Huldah’s husband
people.role: Keeper of the wardrobe
people.relations: Son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah. Husband of Huldah.
people.meaning: He is keeper of the wardrobe. The book names him only as Huldah’s husband.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahikam
people.role: One of the men sent to Huldah
people.relations: Son of Shaphan. Father of Gedaliah.
people.meaning: Josiah commands him and four others to ask the LORD about the book. They go to Huldah the prophetess. They bring her message back to the king.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abdon / Achbor
people.role: One of the men sent to Huldah
people.relations: This book calls him Abdon the son of Micah. Kings calls him Achbor the son of Micaiah.
people.meaning: Josiah sends him with Hilkiah, Ahikam, Shaphan, and Asaiah. They ask Huldah about the book of the law. He does nothing else in the book.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Asaiah
people.role: King’s servant sent to Huldah
people.relations: Called the king’s servant. He serves Josiah.
people.meaning: Josiah sends him with four others after the book is read. They go to Huldah and bring back her message.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joah, son of Joahaz
people.role: Recorder sent to repair the temple
people.relations: Son of Joahaz. Sent with Shaphan and Maaseiah by Josiah.
people.meaning: Josiah sends him to repair the LORD’s house. The three men bring the gathered money to Hilkiah. He is not Joah the son of Asaph, Hezekiah’s recorder in Kings.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Maaseiah, Josiah’s city governor
people.role: City governor sent to repair the temple
people.relations: Governor of the city. Sent with Shaphan and Joah by Josiah.
people.meaning: Josiah sends him to repair the LORD’s house. The three men bring the gathered money to Hilkiah. The workmen use it to buy stone and timber.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pharaoh Neco
people.role: Egyptian king who warns Josiah, then controls Judah
people.relations: King of Egypt. He removes Jehoahaz and makes Jehoiakim king.
people.meaning: He marches to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates. He tells Josiah that God sent him and to stay away. Josiah fights him at Megiddo and is shot. Neco later fines Judah and carries Joahaz to Egypt.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.role: Prophet who laments Josiah and warns Zedekiah
people.relations: He laments Josiah. He speaks the LORD’s word to Zedekiah.
people.meaning: He laments when Josiah dies. Zedekiah does not humble himself before him. The book says the seventy empty years fulfill his word. Cyrus’s order also comes so that his word is done.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Samuel
people.role: Earlier prophet named in a Passover comparison
people.relations: Son of Hannah and Elkanah. Father of Joel and Abijah.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. The book says no Passover like Josiah’s was kept since Samuel’s days.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoahaz, king of Judah
people.role: Josiah’s son removed by Egypt’s king
people.relations: Son of Josiah and Hamutal.
people.meaning: The people of the land make him king after Josiah. He reigns three months. Egypt’s king removes him and fines the land. Neco carries him to Egypt, and the text also spells his name Joahaz.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoiakim
people.role: King of Judah bound by Nebuchadnezzar
people.relations: Son of Josiah and Zebidah. Earlier name Eliakim. Father of Jehoiachin.
people.meaning: Egypt’s king makes him king and changes his name from Eliakim. He does evil for eleven years. Nebuchadnezzar binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon. Some temple vessels go to Babylon too.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoiachin
people.role: King of Judah taken to Babylon
people.relations: Son of Jehoiakim and Nehushta. Nephew of Zedekiah.
people.meaning: He reigns three months and ten days and does evil. Nebuchadnezzar brings him to Babylon with the temple’s valuable vessels. This book says he was eight when he became king. Second Kings 24:8 says eighteen.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zedekiah
people.role: Last king of Judah before Jerusalem falls
people.relations: Kings calls him Josiah’s son and Jehoiachin’s uncle. This book calls him Jehoiachin’s brother (36:10).
people.meaning: Nebuchadnezzar makes him king and makes him swear by God. He does not humble himself before Jeremiah. He rebels against Nebuchadnezzar. Then the Chaldeans burn the temple and carry the people away.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.role: King of Babylon who destroys Jerusalem
people.relations: King of Babylon. He takes Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin and makes Zedekiah king.
people.meaning: He binds Jehoiakim and takes temple vessels to Babylon. He brings Jehoiachin there and makes Zedekiah king. When Zedekiah rebels, his army burns the temple and breaks Jerusalem’s wall. He carries the people who are left to Babylon.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Cyrus
people.role: King of Persia who lets the people go up
people.relations: King of Persia. His order goes through all his kingdom in writing.
people.meaning: In his first year the LORD stirs up his spirit. He says the LORD told him to build a house in Jerusalem. He tells any of the LORD’s people to go up. The book ends with his words.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

places.name: Gibeon
places.summary: God’s Tent of Meeting and Bezalel’s bronze altar stand at Gibeon. Solomon offers there, and God appears to him that night (chapter 1).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Solomon builds the temple here, and Judah’s kings rule from the city. Kings repair or shut the temple in turn. The Chaldeans burn it in chapter 36.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location, not the temple site.

places.name: Kiriath Jearim
places.summary: David had brought God’s ark up from Kiriath Jearim (1:4). He put it in a tent in Jerusalem.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Egypt · broad region
places.summary: Solomon buys horses and chariots from Egypt. Jeroboam flees there, and Shishak comes from there against Rehoboam. Neco later carries Joahaz to Egypt (chapter 36).
places.limits: The marker stands for a whole country, not one point.

places.name: Tyre
places.summary: Huram rules Tyre. He sends Solomon timber and the craftsman Huram-abi (chapter 2).
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Lebanon · broad mountain region
places.summary: Huram’s servants cut cedar, cypress, and algum trees in Lebanon for the temple (chapter 2). Solomon also builds there (8:6).
places.limits: The marker stands for a broad mountain region, not one point.

places.name: Joppa
places.summary: Huram’s men float the timber by sea to Joppa. Solomon’s men carry it up to Jerusalem (2:16).
places.limits: The marker shows the port’s general location.

places.name: Jordan · crossing area uncertain
places.summary: Solomon’s bronze vessels are cast in the plain of the Jordan (4:17). The place is between Succoth and Zeredah.
places.limits: The text gives no exact casting site. The marker shows the river area only.

places.name: Sinai / traditional region
places.summary: Chapter 5 calls the place Horeb. Moses put the two tablets in the ark there. The LORD made a covenant with Israel there (5:10).
places.limits: Scholars dispute which mountain this is. The marker is not a proven site.

places.name: Hamath
places.summary: People come to Solomon’s feast from as far as the entrance of Hamath (7:8). Solomon builds storage cities in Hamath (8:4).
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The “entrance of Hamath” is not a fixed point.

places.name: Beth Horon · upper and lower town region
places.summary: Solomon builds upper and lower Beth Horon as walled cities (8:5). Israel’s sent-back soldiers raid Judah’s cities as far as Beth Horon (25:13).
places.limits: One marker stands for both towns.

places.name: Ezion Geber · disputed Gulf of Aqaba locality
places.summary: Solomon goes to Ezion Geber and Eloth on the seashore in Edom (8:17). Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah build ships there, and the ships are wrecked (chapter 20). Uzziah rebuilds Eloth (26:2).
places.limits: Scholars dispute the exact site near the Gulf of Aqaba. The marker shows the general area.

places.name: Edom · broad region
places.summary: Edom revolts against Jehoram and makes its own king (chapter 21). Amaziah later defeats its men and brings home its gods (chapter 25).
places.limits: The marker stands for a broad region, not one point.

places.name: Sheba · broad southern Arabian reference
places.summary: The queen of Sheba hears of Solomon and comes to test him. Then she returns to her own land (chapter 9).
places.limits: The marker stands for a broad southern Arabian region. It is not her proven capital.

places.name: Shechem
places.summary: All Israel comes to Shechem to make Rehoboam king. He answers them roughly there, and the kingdom splits (chapter 10).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Bethlehem
places.summary: Rehoboam builds Bethlehem as one of Judah’s cities for defense (11:6).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Tekoa
places.summary: Rehoboam builds Tekoa for defense (11:6). Jehoshaphat’s army goes out into the wilderness of Tekoa, singing (20:20).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location. The wilderness around it has no exact edge.

places.name: Adullam · broad locality
places.summary: Rehoboam builds Adullam as one of Judah’s cities for defense (11:7).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Gath · Tell es-Safi
places.summary: Rehoboam builds Gath as a city for defense (11:8). Uzziah later breaks down its wall (26:6).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Lachish
places.summary: Rehoboam builds Lachish for defense (11:9). Amaziah flees there and is killed (25:27). Sennacherib attacks it while his servants go to Jerusalem (32:9).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Hebron
places.summary: Rehoboam builds Hebron as one of Judah’s walled cities (11:10).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Bethel · proposed locality
places.summary: Abijah chases Jeroboam and takes Bethel with its villages (13:19).
places.limits: The site is a proposed one. The marker shows its general location.

places.name: Mareshah
places.summary: Rehoboam builds Mareshah for defense (11:8). Asa meets Zerah’s army there (chapter 14). Eliezer, who warns Jehoshaphat, comes from this town (20:37).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location. The valley of Zephathah is not marked.

places.name: Gerar
places.summary: Asa’s army chases Zerah’s men to Gerar. Judah strikes the cities around it and takes much plunder (14:13–14).
places.limits: Tell Haror is a proposed site. The marker is close, not exact.

places.name: Kidron valley
places.summary: Asa burns Maacah’s image at the brook Kidron (15:16). Hezekiah’s Levites carry temple filth there (chapter 29). The people throw altars into it (chapter 30).
places.limits: The marker shows the valley east of Jerusalem, not an exact spot.

places.name: Damascus
places.summary: Ben Hadad lives at Damascus when Asa pays him (16:2). Syria sends Judah’s plunder and captives there (chapters 24, 28). Ahaz sacrifices to its gods (28:23).
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Ramah · Benjamin locality
places.summary: Baasha builds Ramah to shut Asa in. When he stops, Asa carries off its stones and timber (chapter 16).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location in Benjamin.

places.name: Dan · broad northern locality
places.summary: Ben Hadad’s captains strike Dan (16:4). Hezekiah’s Passover call goes from Beersheba to Dan (30:5).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Mizpah · Benjamin identification uncertain
places.summary: Asa builds Geba and Mizpah with the stones and timber from Ramah (16:6).
places.limits: Scholars are not sure which site in Benjamin is Mizpah. The marker is a proposal.

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: Ahab hosts Jehoshaphat at Samaria, and Micaiah speaks at its gate (chapter 18). Ahaziah hides there (22:9). Oded meets Israel’s army there, and the captives go free (chapter 28).
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Ramoth Gilead · locality disputed
places.summary: Ahab and Jehoshaphat fight Syria at Ramoth Gilead, and Ahab dies (chapter 18). The Syrians wound Joram there (22:5).
places.limits: Scholars dispute the site. The marker shows one general area.

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Jehoshaphat goes among the people from Beersheba to Ephraim’s hills (19:4). Zibiah, mother of Joash, comes from Beersheba (24:1). Hezekiah’s Passover call starts there (30:5).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: En Gedi
places.summary: Messengers tell Jehoshaphat that a great army is at Hazazon Tamar. The text says that is En Gedi (20:2).
places.limits: The marker shows the general location, not the army’s camp.

places.name: Moab · broad region
places.summary: The children of Moab come with Ammon against Jehoshaphat. The armies then destroy each other (chapter 20).
places.limits: The marker stands for a broad region, not one point.

places.name: Libnah · site uncertain
places.summary: Libnah revolts against Jehoram when Edom does. The book says he had left the LORD (21:10).
places.limits: Scholars dispute where Libnah was. The marker is a proposal.

places.name: Jezreel
places.summary: The wounded Joram goes to Jezreel to heal. Ahaziah of Judah visits him there (22:6).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Beth Shemesh · proposed Ain Shems locality
places.summary: Joash of Israel defeats and captures Amaziah at Beth Shemesh (chapter 25). The Philistines take the town in the days of Ahaz (28:18).
places.limits: Ain Shems is a proposed site. The marker shows the town, not the battle spot.

places.name: Ashdod
places.summary: Uzziah breaks down the wall of Ashdod. He builds cities in its country (26:6).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Four leaders of Ephraim bring Judah’s freed captives to Jericho, to their brothers. The text calls it the city of palm trees (28:15).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Assyria · broad northern Mesopotamian region
places.summary: Ahaz sends to Assyria’s kings for help and gets trouble (chapter 28). Sennacherib comes from Assyria against Judah (chapter 32). Its captains take Manasseh away (33:11).
places.limits: The marker stands for a broad region, not one point.

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: Princes of Babylon send men to Hezekiah (32:31). Manasseh is carried there and returns (chapter 33). Nebuchadnezzar takes kings, vessels, and people there (chapter 36).
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Megiddo
places.summary: Josiah fights Neco in the valley of Megiddo. Archers shoot him there (35:22–23).
places.limits: The marker shows the town, not the battle spot in the valley.

places.name: Carchemish
places.summary: Neco goes up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates. Josiah goes out against him on the way (35:20).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

contextGuide.title: 2 Chronicles: context and evidence
contextGuide.description: Explore the book’s larger concerns through selected passages and relevant evidence.

steps.title: Water and metal serve different tasks
steps.text: Verse 6 separates two uses of water. The ten basins wash the parts of the burnt offerings. The sea is for the priests to wash in. Exodus 30:18–21 required priests to wash before serving. The tabernacle had one lampstand and one table, and the temple has ten. The text describes the objects by the work they do. Regional metalwork offers comparison without reconstructing these exact vessels.

steps.title: Defense combines work and trust
steps.text: Hezekiah’s first response is practical. He blocks the water an army would need (verses 3–4). Verse 5 lists a repaired wall, towers, a second wall, and weapons. His speech in verses 7–8 then asks the people to trust God. The account sets defense and prayer together. Assyrian records describe the campaign from the attacking king’s side. Chronicles leaves out the tribute reported in 2 Kings 18:14–16.

steps.title: The last royal speech opens a road beyond exile
steps.text: Verses 15–16 explain the exile before verse 23 ends it. God sent messengers out of compassion, and they were mocked. The final speech comes from Cyrus, a foreign ruler. It allows a return and the rebuilding of a temple. The book’s last words are “let him go up.” The Cyrus Cylinder gives wider context for Persian restoration claims. It does not name this return or prove every detail of the speech.
